WITH reporter_incidents AS (

        o.employee_id,
        MAX(o.employee_name) AS employee_name,

hybrid_sub_results.question: Using pre-extracted facts F-OC-02, F-AUTO-08B54491BA, and F-AUTO-14E5B8B6B3, summarize what the OnCall Runbook says about response-time SLAs; additionally retrieve any OnCall Runbook guidance specifically about burnout, fatigue, workload rotation, or escalation/coverage practices related to burnout risk.
hybrid_sub_results.answer:
From the OnCall Runbook, the response-time SLAs are:

- For routine on-call paging, the **primary on-call must acknowledge pages within 5 minutes during business hours (09:00–21:00 IST)** and **within 15 minutes during off-hours**. If they do not acknowledge in time, the page **automatically escalates to the secondary on-call**. The runbook also says each team maintains both a **primary and secondary on-call engineer** on a weekly rotation. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]
- For incident severity response targets, the runbook defines:
  - **SEV-1:** response in **5 minutes**
  - **SEV-2:** response in **15 minutes**
  - **SEV-3:** response in **30 minutes**
  - **SEV-4:** response by the **next business day** [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec2]

On burnout, fatigue, workload rotation, and escalation/coverage practices, the OnCall Runbook guidance I found is:

- **Weekly rotation structure:** on-call runs on a **weekly schedule** from **Monday 09:00 IST to the following Monday 09:00 IST**, which is the workload rotation mechanism described in the runbook. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]
- **Coverage model to reduce single-person risk:** each team has both a **primary and secondary on-call engineer**, and missed acknowledgments by the primary **trigger automatic escalation to the secondary**, which is the clearest burnout-risk-related coverage practice in the document. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]
- **Fatigue / overload relief:** if an engineer is **paged more than 3 times during off-hours in a single week**, they are **entitled to a compensatory day off within 30 days**. This is the only explicit burnout/fatigue mitigation guidance I found in the OnCall Runbook. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]

I do not find additional OnCall Runbook guidance specifically mentioning “burnout,” “fatigue,” or broader workload-balancing practices beyond the weekly rotation, secondary coverage/escalation, and comp-off rule above. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]

hybrid_sub_results.answer:
The standard policy for locking in critical talent is that **HR may offer a retention bonus of up to 30% of annual CTC without additional approvals**, but this applies specifically to **critical talent identified via the 9-box grid as high-potential/high-performance**. That is the default approval posture for standard retention actions. [TechNova_Salary_Structure.pdf::sec5]

Related approval posture in the same policy distinguishes this from **counter-offers**: for employees with competing offers, **VP-level approval** is needed for adjustments **up to 25%**, and **C-suite approval** is required for adjustments **above 25%**; the **maximum counter-offer is capped at 40% above current CTC**. [TechNova_Salary_Structure.pdf::sec5]

This same 30% figure is also reflected elsewhere as the policy cap for retention bonuses tied to talent-retention risk. [TechNova_DRHP_Draft.pdf::sec4]

hybrid_sub_results.question: Using pre-extracted facts F-OC-02, F-AUTO-08B54491BA, and F-AUTO-14E5B8B6B3, summarize what the OnCall Runbook says about response-time SLAs; additionally retrieve any OnCall Runbook guidance specifically about burnout, fatigue, workload rotation, or escalation/coverage practices related to burnout risk.
hybrid_sub_results.answer:
From the OnCall Runbook, the response-time SLAs are:

- For routine on-call paging, the **primary on-call must acknowledge pages within 5 minutes during business hours (09:00–21:00 IST)** and **within 15 minutes during off-hours**. If they do not acknowledge in time, the page **automatically escalates to the secondary on-call**. The runbook also says each team maintains both a **primary and secondary on-call engineer** on a weekly rotation. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]
- For incident severity response targets, the runbook defines:
  - **SEV-1:** response in **5 minutes**
  - **SEV-2:** response in **15 minutes**
  - **SEV-3:** response in **30 minutes**
  - **SEV-4:** response by the **next business day** [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec2]

On burnout, fatigue, workload rotation, and escalation/coverage practices, the OnCall Runbook guidance I found is:

- **Weekly rotation structure:** on-call runs on a **weekly schedule** from **Monday 09:00 IST to the following Monday 09:00 IST**, which is the workload rotation mechanism described in the runbook. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]
- **Coverage model to reduce single-person risk:** each team has both a **primary and secondary on-call engineer**, and missed acknowledgments by the primary **trigger automatic escalation to the secondary**, which is the clearest burnout-risk-related coverage practice in the document. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]
- **Fatigue / overload relief:** if an engineer is **paged more than 3 times during off-hours in a single week**, they are **entitled to a compensatory day off within 30 days**. This is the only explicit burnout/fatigue mitigation guidance I found in the OnCall Runbook. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]

I do not find additional OnCall Runbook guidance specifically mentioning “burnout,” “fatigue,” or broader workload-balancing practices beyond the weekly rotation, secondary coverage/escalation, and comp-off rule above. [TechNova_OnCall_Runbook.pdf::sec1]

hybrid_sub_results.question: Using pre-extracted facts F-SAL-03, F-AUTO-42748ED1A6, and F-AUTO-6117CA66E7, summarize the standard retention policy applicable to locking in critical talent, including the 30% of annual CTC cap and approval posture.
hybrid_sub_results.answer:
The standard policy for locking in critical talent is that **HR may offer a retention bonus of up to 30% of annual CTC without additional approvals**, but this applies specifically to **critical talent identified via the 9-box grid as high-potential/high-performance**. That is the default approval posture for standard retention actions. [TechNova_Salary_Structure.pdf::sec5]

Related approval posture in the same policy distinguishes this from **counter-offers**: for employees with competing offers, **VP-level approval** is needed for adjustments **up to 25%**, and **C-suite approval** is required for adjustments **above 25%**; the **maximum counter-offer is capped at 40% above current CTC**. [TechNova_Salary_Structure.pdf::sec5]

This same 30% figure is also reflected elsewhere as the policy cap for retention bonuses tied to talent-retention risk. [TechNova_DRHP_Draft.pdf::sec4]
